Q: Better algorithm to find the maximum number whose square divides K A:

The greatest square divisor of K can be found easily if you have the prime factorization of K. However, this is an expensive operation, but if you already know K = A*B for known A and B, the factorizations of A and B can then easily be combined to give the prime factorization of K. For

K = prod_{p prime | K} p_i^{e_i}

gsd(K) = prod_{p prime | K} p_i^{e_i - {e_i & 1}}

where {e_i & 1} is 1 when e_i is odd, and zero otherwise.

For sufficently small integers, e.g. 64 bit, the radical can be computed efficiently by trial division up to the cube root without requiring knowledge of the complete prime factorization. See Algorithm For Largest Square-Free Divisor (a.k.a. Radical) Of An Integer. Suppose you know the radicals of A and B, then

rad = radical(K) = radical(A)*radical(B) / gcd(radical(A), radical(B))

The greatest square divisor of K can be computed efficiently from the radical using the following algorithm.

function gsdfromradical(K, rad) {
  if (K <= 1) return K
  w = gcd(rad, K/rad)
  v = K
  u = 2
  while (u > 1) 
    u = gcd(v, w)
    v /= u
  x = K/(v*w*w)
  if (x == 1) return w*w
  return w*w*(gsdfromradical(x, gcd(rad, x)))


Then you can factorise g = isqrt(gsdfromradical(K, radical(K))), make an ordered list of all divisors of g, and the final answer is the largest divisor <= min(A,B).

Q: flextable and officedown error: read_docx only support docx files A:

I saw this post that had the same error about read_docx when using flextable. The problem is most possibly from the filepath!

I have fixed my problem because I finally found a space in my username so the filepath of templated generated by officedown will be copied to C:\Users\Myfirstname Mygivenname\AppData\something_else. Then in terminal it will be C:\Users\Myfirstname~Mygivenname\AppData\something_else and get wrong. This is may be the question for Windows users as I have tried the same thing on my Mac and it works.

So make sure that your username (or the entire filepath) does not have any space!

Q: Keep old TabView style in iOS / iPadOS 18.1 A:

You can call this method at the start of your app lifecycle (in SwiftUI you'd need to use an App Delegate depending on how early your tab bar view appears):

UserDefaults.standard.register(defaults: ["UseFloatingTabBar": false])

This will give you the old-style tab bar. On iOS 18 it will stretch across the device (like it used to on iOS 17) but on iOS 26 it will be only as wide as it needs to be.

This also works with modern tab bar features such as the separate inline search.

This is an internal flag within the system similar to defaults write on macOS. That means it is officially unsupported and could be removed in a future version of iPadOS but the risks are manageable. I have used it in several production apps since the launch of iPadOS 18 in 2024 and have never had any issues with App Review. The fact that they redesigned this component for Liquid Glass makes me fairly confident it won’t be removed anytime soon.

-- https://bendodson.com/weblog/2026/01/22/traditional-tab-bar-on-ipados-26/
